chunks: Ibn al-Nadim said in al-Fihrist: '(Abu Abdallah — in our era the leadership of the Shia theologians has come to rest with him; he is foremost in the craft of kalam according to the school of his companions, of subtle perception and sharp-mindedness — I observed him and found him to be brilliant...)'
He also said in another place: '(In our time, the leadership of his companions from the Imami Shia has come to rest with him — in fiqh, kalam, and the transmitted traditions...)'

key_terms.رِئَاسَةُ: leadership, headship of a scholarly community

ai.seo_question: What did Ibn al-Nadim write in al-Fihrist about Sheikh al-Mufid's leadership in Shia kalam and fiqh?
ai.summary: Ibn al-Nadim, in his encyclopedic al-Fihrist, identifies Abu Abdallah (Sheikh al-Mufid) as the supreme head of Shia theologians in his era, praising his unrivalled mastery of kalam, subtlety of perception, and razor-sharp intellect, adding that he personally witnessed his brilliance. In a second passage he reaffirms that leadership of the Imami Shia in fiqh, kalam, and transmitted traditions had come to rest with him.
